claims.text: What the image looks like Effaced 4th ventricle, posterior fossa hyperdensity → cerebellar hemorrhage
claims.quote: Effaced 4th ventricle, posterior fossa hyperdensity Cerebellar hemorrhage

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Confirm it is non-contrast (so blood/calcium is not confused with contrast)
claims.quote: Confirm non-contrast (so blood/calcium not confused with contrast).

claims.text: Symmetry: gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns
claims.quote: Symmetry - gray-white differentiation, ventricles, sulci, basal cisterns.

claims.text: Blood: look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH)
claims.quote: Blood - look for hyperdensity 60-80 HU (epidural / subdural / SAH / IPH / IVH).

claims.text: Brain: gray-white preservation; look for sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift
claims.quote: Brain - gray-white preservation, sulcal effacement, mass effect, midline shift.

claims.text: Cisterns: basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk
claims.quote: Cisterns - basal/suprasellar (5-pointed star); effaced = herniation risk.

claims.text: Ventricles: symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus
claims.quote: Ventricles - symmetric size; trapped temporal horn = early hydrocephalus.

claims.text: Cerebellar hematomas can expand to block the 4th ventricle, causing acute hydrocephalus, or dissect into the brain stem; those > 3 cm in diameter may cause midline shift or herniation
claims.quote: Cerebellar hematomas can expand to block the 4th ventricle, also causing acute hydrocephalus, or they can dissect into the brain stem. Cerebellar hematomas that are > 3 cm in diameter may cause midline shift or herniation.

claims.text: Causes Intracerebral hemorrhage usually results from rupture of an arteriosclerotic small artery weakened primarily by chronic arterial hypertension
claims.quote: Intracerebral hemorrhage usually results from rupture of an arteriosclerotic small artery that has been weakened, primarily by chronic arterial hypertension.

claims.text: Symptoms Large hemorrhages in the posterior fossa cause cerebellar or brain stem deficits (eg, conjugate eye deviation or ophthalmoplegia, stertorous breathing, pinpoint pupils, coma)
claims.quote: Large hemorrhages, when located in the hemispheres, cause hemiparesis; when located in the posterior fossa, they cause cerebellar or brain stem deficits (eg, conjugate eye deviation or ophthalmoplegia, stertorous breathing, pinpoint pupils, coma).

claims.text: Herniation, midbrain or pontine hemorrhage, intraventricular hemorrhage, acute hydrocephalus or dissection into the brain stem can impair consciousness and cause coma and death
claims.quote: Herniation, midbrain or pontine hemorrhage, intraventricular hemorrhage, acute hydrocephalus, or dissection into the brain stem can impair consciousness and cause coma and death.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: surgical evacuation if >3 cm or brainstem compression
claims.quote: Surgical evacuation if >3 cm or brainstem compression

claims.text: Cerebellar hemisphere hematomas > 3 cm in diameter may cause midline shift or herniation, so surgical evacuation is often lifesaving
claims.quote: Cerebellar hemisphere hematomas that are > 3 cm in diameter may cause midline shift or herniation, so surgical evacuation is often lifesaving.

claims.text: Consider surgical evacuation for hematomas > 3 cm in a cerebellar hemisphere, and an external ventricular drain for select patients with signs of hydrocephalus and increased intracerebral pressure
claims.quote: Consider surgical evacuation for large lobar cerebral hematomas and hematomas > 3 cm in a cerebellar hemisphere. Consider placing an external ventricular drain for select patients with signs of hydrocephalus and increased intracerebral pressure.
